screening_decisions.reason: RCT design with COPD patients aged 60+ (meets >40 criterion). Anxiety measured using SCL (validated scale). Intervention is nurse-led Minimal Psychological Intervention based on CBT principles (psychological therapy). Comparison is usual care - while not strictly 'no intervention or education only', the conservative approach warrants inclusion given the study meets most other criteria and usual care may include education components.
Cross-sectional study using principal component analysis to identify anxiety symptom clusters. Not an RCT, cluster-randomised trial, or cross-over trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
Theoretical/academic paper about psychiatric training framework. Not an RCT and does not involve COPD patients. Does not meet study design or population criteria.
Methodological paper about psychophysical rating methods. Not an RCT and does not involve COPD patients with anxiety. Does not meet study design or population criteria.

RCT with chronic breathing disorder patients. PMR is a psychological therapy. However, comparison group received full pulmonary rehabilitation (exercise, education, psychosocial support) - not 'no intervention or education only'. The intervention was added to standard care, and there was no group receiving co-intervention alone.
Case control study about personality disorder patients, not COPD. Not an RCT. Does not meet study design or population criteria.
RCT with COPD patients. However, intervention is acupressure (physical/complementary therapy), not a psychological therapy. Does not meet intervention criteria.
Review article summarizing literature on anxiety in COPD. Not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
Cross-sectional study assessing prevalence of anxiety/depression in COPD. Not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
RCT with COPD patients. However, interventions are activity training and lecture series added to exercise training - these are not psychological therapies. Does not meet intervention criteria.
Guidelines document from GOLD initiative. Not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
Cross-sectional study examining risk factors for anxiety/depression in COPD. Not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
Single-blinded study testing fluoxetine (antidepressant drug). Intervention is pharmacological, not psychological therapy. Does not meet intervention criteria.

RCT with COPD patients and psychotherapy intervention. However, comparison groups received either exercise alone or psychotherapy alone - no group received 'no intervention or education only'. The co-intervention criterion is not met as there's no group receiving the co-intervention (exercise) alone without psychotherapy as a proper comparison.
Methodological paper describing a questionnaire for measuring quality of life in airways disease. Not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
Cross-sectional analysis from INSPIRE-II trial examining associations between anxiety/depression and COPD symptoms. Not an RCT of psychological therapy. Does not meet study design criteria.
Methodological paper about meta-analysis inconsistency measurement. Not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
Study protocol for a planned RCT, not a completed study with results. No outcomes reported. Does not meet criteria for inclusion as it's a protocol document.
Cochrane review protocol about pharmacological interventions for anxiety in COPD. Intervention is pharmacological, not psychological therapy. Does not meet intervention criteria.
Cross-sectional study with factorial design examining HRV responses to stress in COPD patients with anxiety. Not an RCT of psychological therapy. Does not meet study design criteria.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. The study design does not meet the inclusion criteria which requires randomised controlled trials, cluster-randomised trials, or cross-over trials.
This is a methodological/statistical note about units of analysis in clinical research. It is not an RCT and does not address psychological therapies for anxiety in COPD patients.
This is a qualitative study using in-depth interviews with 14 patients. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate a psychological therapy intervention.
This is a workshop proceedings report summarizing current understanding and future research needs. It is not an RCT evaluating psychological therapies.
This is a cross-sectional observational study examining relationships between functional status and psychopathology. It is not an RCT and does not test a psychological therapy intervention.
This is a review article addressing diagnosis, epidemiology, theoretical conceptualizations, and treatment recommendations. It is not an RCT.

This is an RCT testing CBT for anxiety and depression in COPD patients. Uses validated measures (Beck Anxiety Inventory). However, the control group received 'enhanced standard care' rather than no intervention or education only, which creates uncertainty about meeting the comparison criteria. Included conservatively pending full-text review.
This is a systematic review examining psychological interventions. While it discusses RCTs, it is itself a review article, not a primary RCT.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal observational studies examining associations between anxiety/depression and COPD outcomes. It is not an RCT evaluating psychological therapies.
This is a cross-sectional survey study examining the relationship between social support and anxiety. It is not an RCT and does not test a psychological therapy intervention.
This is a methodological paper about sample size calculations for cluster-randomised trials. It is not an RCT evaluating psychological therapies for anxiety in COPD.

This is an RCT testing a telephone-based coping skills intervention (psychological therapy) vs COPD education in COPD patients. Anxiety was measured as an outcome. The comparison group received education only, which meets the criteria. Age range (38-81) includes some under 40, but majority likely over 40. Included conservatively.
This is a narrative review article discussing depression in COPD and summarizing evidence from various trials. It is not a primary RCT evaluating psychological therapies for anxiety.

This is an RCT testing CBT for preventing panic attacks and anxiety symptoms in COPD patients who had undergone pulmonary rehabilitation. Primary outcomes included panic attacks, panic disorder, and anxiety symptoms. The control group received routine care. Uncertainty exists about whether routine care qualifies as 'no intervention or education only'. Included conservatively pending full-text review.
This is a prospective observational cohort study examining risk factors for rehospitalization. It is not an RCT and does not test a psychological therapy intervention.

This is an RCT testing a taped relaxation message (psychological therapy) for reducing anxiety in COPD patients. The control group was instructed to sit quietly, which approximates no intervention. Anxiety was measured as an outcome. Meets key inclusion criteria.
This is a cohort study examining the relationship between anxiety and health outcomes in COPD. It is not an RCT and does not test a psychological therapy intervention.
This is a narrative review providing an overview of depression and anxiety in COPD. It is not a primary RCT evaluating psychological therapies.
This appears to be a commentary or opinion piece about anxiety recognition in COPD. It is not an RCT evaluating psychological therapies.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs examining psychological and lifestyle interventions. While it analyzes RCTs, it is itself a review article, not a primary RCT.

This is an observational/correlational study using path analysis to test a model of variables influencing functional status in COPD. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate a psychological therapy intervention.

RCT comparing CBT group treatment with COPD education for COPD patients with moderate-to-severe anxiety/depressive symptoms assessed using validated scales (BAI, BDI-II). Meets all criteria: RCT design, COPD population with anxiety, psychological therapy intervention, education-only comparison.

RCT evaluating psychotherapy added to pulmonary rehabilitation program. Both groups received exercise and physiotherapy; experimental group additionally received psychotherapy sessions. Control group received co-interventions (exercise, physiotherapy) without psychotherapy, satisfying the co-intervention rule. Anxiety assessed using BAI (validated scale).
This is a normative study reporting community norms for anxiety questionnaires. It is not an RCT and does not involve COPD patients or psychological therapy interventions.

While this is an RCT of a stress management program, the population includes both obstructive AND restrictive pulmonary disease (not COPD-specific). Additionally, there is no clear indication that participants had confirmed anxiety disorders via diagnostic criteria or validated scales.
This is a review article discussing pathophysiologic relationships between panic, anxiety, and respiratory disease. It is not an RCT.
This is a cross-sectional survey study examining COPD-related fears and disability. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate a psychological therapy intervention.
This is a psychometric validation study of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. It is not an RCT and does not involve COPD patients or psychological therapy interventions.

While this is an RCT, the primary intervention is comprehensive pulmonary rehabilitation (exercise training, education, physical care) with psychosocial support as only one component. The main focus is not psychological therapy for anxiety disorders.
This is a review article summarizing literature on anxiety and depression in COPD. It is not an RCT.
This is a methodology study comparing different walking tests for exercise tolerance. It is not an RCT and does not involve psychological therapy interventions.
This is a theoretical/review paper discussing connections between panic disorder and respiration. It is not an RCT.

This is an observational/correlational study examining relationships between emotional factors and daily impairment in COPD. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate a psychological therapy intervention.
This is a cross-sectional prevalence study validating the BASDEC screening questionnaire. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate a psychological therapy intervention.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of psychological interventions in COPD. While relevant to the topic, it is not a primary RCT.
This is a critical review of literature on psychological distress and COPD exacerbations. It is not an RCT.
This is a review article on anxiety in pulmonary disease covering epidemiology, comorbidity, diagnosis, and treatment. It is not an RCT.

Single-blind RCT comparing 2-hour CBT group session with COPD education for elderly COPD patients. Anxiety assessed using Beck Anxiety Inventory (validated scale). Meets all criteria: RCT design, COPD population with anxiety symptoms, psychological therapy intervention, education-only comparison.
